## Objective

Stage 8 consolidates the baseline (Stage 6) and hyperparameter-tuned (Stage 7) results, compares the candidate models on consistent metrics, quantifies the effect of tuning, produces the comparative visuals Phase 2 calls for (ROC, Precision-Recall, confusion matrices, feature importance), and fixes the model candidates carried into Phase 3.

Only the `validation` split is used here. `crc_calibration`, `iid_holdout` and `future_test` are not touched in this stage. Because `validation` was also used for tuning (including XGBoost early stopping), the tuned metrics are mildly optimistic, and Phase 3 must calibrate on `crc_calibration`.

## Setup

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = TRUE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath("."))
source(file.path("R", "00_setup.R"))
library(data.table); library(ggplot2); library(DBI); library(RSQLite); library(glmnet)
# glmnet must be loaded (not just installed) for coef(en_fit$model, ...) below to
# dispatch to coef.glmnet() -- without it, the bare generic call silently falls
# through to coef.default(), which doesn't understand a glmnet object and
# returns nothing usable (this was the cause of the Elastic-Net importance
# WARN: "'data' must be of a vector type, was 'NULL'").
data.table::setDTthreads(2)
set.seed(20260917)

# Settings fixed BEFORE looking at results
N_BOOT           <- 200     # paired bootstrap replicates
SELECTION_MARGIN <- 0.005   # keep a full-validation model if within this AUC of the best

FIGURE_DIR <- if (exists("FIGURE_DIR")) FIGURE_DIR else file.path("outputs", "figures")
dir.create(FIGURE_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
MODEL_ZOO_TUNED_DIR <- file.path(MODEL_DIR, "model_zoo_tuned")
DB_PATH <- file.path("data", "costconformal_return.sqlite")
```

```{r helpers}
# Same metric definition as Stage 7
compute_metrics <- function(y, p) {
  p <- pmin(pmax(p, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6)
  cls <- as.integer(p >= 0.5)
  tp <- sum(cls == 1 & y == 1); fp <- sum(cls == 1 & y == 0)
  tn <- sum(cls == 0 & y == 0); fn <- sum(cls == 0 & y == 1)
  prec <- if ((tp + fp) == 0) NA_real_ else tp / (tp + fp)
  rec  <- if ((tp + fn) == 0) NA_real_ else tp / (tp + fn)
  f1   <- if (is.na(prec) || is.na(rec) || (prec + rec) == 0) NA_real_ else 2 * prec * rec / (prec + rec)
  data.table(auc = auc_roc(y, p), pr_auc = pr_auc(y, p), brier = brier_score(y, p),
             log_loss = log_loss(y, p), accuracy = (tp + tn) / length(y),
             precision = prec, recall = rec, f1 = f1)
}

# Rank-based AUC, fast enough for bootstrapping.
# FIX: n1/n0 were plain integers -- on ~205k full-validation rows (n1 ~
# 113,000, n0 ~ 92,000), n1 * n0 ~ 10.4 billion overflows R's 32-bit integer
# (max ~2.147 billion), silently producing NA. This was invisible on small
# samples but guaranteed every one of the 200 bootstrap replicates below to
# return NA for every full-validation model, which would have crashed
# quantile() on an all-NA vector. Casting to double before multiplying fixes
# it the same way auc_roc() itself was fixed earlier in this project --
# double multiplication doesn't overflow until ~9e15, far beyond this scale.
fast_auc <- function(y, p) {
  r <- data.table::frank(p, ties.method = "average")
  n1 <- as.double(sum(y == 1)); n0 <- as.double(sum(y == 0))
  (sum(r[y == 1]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * n0)
}

# Threshold-swept ROC/PR curve points, used only for the two overlay plots
# below (not for any AUC number itself -- those come from auc_roc()/fast_auc()).
roc_curve_points <- function(y, p, n_points = 200) {
  thresholds <- seq(1, 0, length.out = n_points)
  rbindlist(lapply(thresholds, function(t) {
    pred <- as.integer(p >= t)
    tp <- sum(pred == 1 & y == 1); fp <- sum(pred == 1 & y == 0)
    tn <- sum(pred == 0 & y == 0); fn <- sum(pred == 0 & y == 1)
    data.table(threshold = t, tpr = tp / (tp + fn), fpr = fp / (fp + tn))
  }))
}
pr_curve_points <- function(y, p, n_points = 200) {
  thresholds <- seq(1, 0, length.out = n_points)
  rbindlist(lapply(thresholds, function(t) {
    pred <- as.integer(p >= t)
    tp <- sum(pred == 1 & y == 1); fp <- sum(pred == 1 & y == 0); fn <- sum(pred == 0 & y == 1)
    data.table(threshold = t,
               precision = if ((tp + fp) == 0) NA_real_ else tp / (tp + fp),
               recall = if ((tp + fn) == 0) NA_real_ else tp / (tp + fn))
  }))
}
```

## Load Stage 6 and Stage 7 outputs

```{r load}
baseline_leaderboard <- fread(file.path(TABLE_DIR, "model_zoo_01_leaderboard.csv"))
stage7_comparison    <- fread(file.path(TABLE_DIR, "tune_05_baseline_vs_tuned.csv"))
preds <- fread(file.path(PROCESSED_DIR, "model_zoo_validation_predictions.csv.gz"))

if ("isReturned" %in% names(preds)) {
  y <- preds$isReturned
} else {
  # Defensive fallback only -- preds$isReturned should always exist (Stage 6
  # writes it). ORDER BY rowid makes the row-order assumption explicit rather
  # than silently relying on SQLite's insertion-order behavior.
  con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), DB_PATH)
  y <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT isReturned FROM validation ORDER BY rowid")$isReturned
  DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
}
stopifnot(length(y) == nrow(preds))   # row order must match Stage 7's validation order
cat("Validation rows:", length(y), "| return rate:", round(mean(y), 4), "\n")

models <- data.table(
  model_id   = c("xgboost", "elastic_net_logistic", "random_forest", "knn"),
  label      = c("XGBoost", "Elastic-Net", "Random Forest", "KNN"),
  tuned_col  = c("prob_xgboost_tuned", "prob_elastic_net_logistic_tuned",
                 "prob_random_forest_tuned", "prob_knn_tuned"),
  model_path = file.path(MODEL_ZOO_TUNED_DIR,
                         c("xgboost_tuned.rds", "elastic_net_logistic_tuned.rds",
                           "random_forest_tuned.rds", "knn_tuned.rds"))
)
stopifnot(all(models$tuned_col %in% names(preds)))
```

## Tuned metrics

Each model is scored on the rows it was actually evaluated on. KNN has probabilities for only a 5,000-row validation subsample; the other three cover the full validation split.

```{r tuned-metrics}
tuned_metrics <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(models)), function(i) {
  p <- preds[[models$tuned_col[i]]]
  keep <- which(!is.na(p))
  m <- compute_metrics(y[keep], p[keep])
  m[, `:=`(model_id = models$model_id[i], n_eval = length(keep),
           evaluated_on = if (length(keep) < length(y)) "validation subsample" else "full validation")]
  m
}))
knitr::kable(tuned_metrics[, .(model_id, n_eval, evaluated_on, auc, pr_auc, brier, log_loss)],
             digits = 4, caption = "Tuned models, each on its own evaluation rows")
```

### Like-for-like check on the KNN subsample

```{r common-subset}
knn_rows <- which(!is.na(preds$prob_knn_tuned))
common_subset <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(models)), function(i) {
  m <- compute_metrics(y[knn_rows], preds[[models$tuned_col[i]]][knn_rows])
  m[, `:=`(model_id = models$model_id[i], n_eval = length(knn_rows))]
  m
}))
knitr::kable(common_subset[, .(model_id, n_eval, auc, pr_auc, brier)], digits = 4,
             caption = "All four tuned models scored on the same 5,000 rows")

# Was the Stage 6 KNN baseline scored on the same rows?
knn_baseline_check <- NULL
if ("prob_knn" %in% names(preds) && any(!is.na(preds$prob_knn))) {
  kr <- which(!is.na(preds$prob_knn))
  knn_baseline_check <- data.table(
    baseline_rows = length(kr), tuned_rows = length(knn_rows),
    same_rows = identical(kr, knn_rows),
    baseline_auc_recomputed = auc_roc(y[kr], preds$prob_knn[kr]))
  print(knn_baseline_check)
} else {
  cat("NOTE: no baseline KNN probabilities in the predictions file; cannot verify that the",
      "Stage 6 KNN baseline used the same rows as the tuned KNN.\n")
}
```

## Baseline vs tuned

```{r comparison}
base_cols <- intersect(c("model_id", "auc", "pr_auc", "brier"), names(baseline_leaderboard))
base <- baseline_leaderboard[model_id %in% models$model_id, ..base_cols]
setnames(base, setdiff(base_cols, "model_id"), paste0("baseline_", setdiff(base_cols, "model_id")))

tuned <- tuned_metrics[, .(model_id, tuned_auc = auc, tuned_pr_auc = pr_auc,
                           tuned_brier = brier, tuned_log_loss = log_loss,
                           n_eval, evaluated_on)]
comparison <- merge(base, tuned, by = "model_id")
comparison <- merge(comparison, stage7_comparison[, .(model_id, hyperparameters)], by = "model_id")
comparison[, `:=`(auc_delta = tuned_auc - baseline_auc, brier_delta = tuned_brier - baseline_brier)]
if ("baseline_pr_auc" %in% names(comparison)) comparison[, pr_auc_delta := tuned_pr_auc - baseline_pr_auc]
comparison <- merge(comparison, models[, .(model_id, label)], by = "model_id")
setorder(comparison, -tuned_auc)

knitr::kable(comparison[, .(label, baseline_auc, tuned_auc, auc_delta,
                            baseline_brier, tuned_brier, brier_delta, evaluated_on)],
             digits = 5, caption = "Baseline vs tuned (KNN is a subsample result)")
```

## Paired bootstrap on full-validation models

The gaps between the top models are small, so a paired bootstrap (the same resampled rows for every model) gives an interval for each AUC gap to the best model.

```{r bootstrap}
full_ids <- tuned_metrics[evaluated_on == "full validation"][order(-auc), model_id]
P <- sapply(full_ids, function(id) preds[[models[model_id == id, tuned_col]]])
best_id <- full_ids[1]
n <- length(y)

boot_auc <- matrix(NA_real_, N_BOOT, length(full_ids), dimnames = list(NULL, full_ids))
for (b in seq_len(N_BOOT)) {
  idx <- sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE)
  for (j in seq_along(full_ids)) boot_auc[b, j] <- fast_auc(y[idx], P[idx, j])
}

boot_tbl <- rbindlist(lapply(setdiff(full_ids, best_id), function(id) {
  d <- boot_auc[, best_id] - boot_auc[, id]
  data.table(model_id = id, best_model = best_id, auc_gap = mean(d),
             gap_ci_low = quantile(d, 0.025), gap_ci_high = quantile(d, 0.975))
}))
knitr::kable(boot_tbl, digits = 5, caption = "AUC gap to the best model, 95% paired-bootstrap interval")
```

## Final selection

Rule (fixed in advance): a model moves to Phase 3 if it was scored on full validation and its AUC is within `r SELECTION_MARGIN` of the best model. Models evaluated only on the KNN subsample are not eligible.

```{r selection}
selection <- merge(tuned_metrics[, .(model_id, auc, pr_auc, brier, n_eval, evaluated_on)],
                   models[, .(model_id, label)], by = "model_id")
best_auc <- max(selection[evaluated_on == "full validation", auc])
selection[, delta_vs_best := best_auc - auc]
selection[, selected := evaluated_on == "full validation" & delta_vs_best <= SELECTION_MARGIN]
selection[, reason := fifelse(
  selected & delta_vs_best == 0, "Highest validation AUC",
  fifelse(selected, paste0("Within ", SELECTION_MARGIN, " AUC of best; distinct model family"),
          fifelse(evaluated_on != "full validation",
                  "Evaluated on 5,000-row subsample only and far below the others; excluded from Phase 3",
                  "More than the selection margin below best")))]
selection <- merge(selection, boot_tbl[, .(model_id, gap_ci_low, gap_ci_high)], by = "model_id", all.x = TRUE)
setorder(selection, -auc)
knitr::kable(selection[, .(label, auc, delta_vs_best, gap_ci_low, gap_ci_high, selected, reason)],
             digits = 5, caption = "Phase-2 model selection (validation only)")
```

## How flat were the tuning grids?

```{r tuning-summary}
grid_files <- c(elastic_net_logistic = "tune_01_elastic_net_grid.csv", knn = "tune_02_knn_grid.csv",
                random_forest = "tune_03_random_forest_grid.csv", xgboost = "tune_04_xgboost_grid.csv")
tuning_summary <- rbindlist(lapply(names(grid_files), function(m) {
  g <- fread(file.path(TABLE_DIR, grid_files[[m]]))
  data.table(model_id = m, n_configs = nrow(g), best_auc = max(g$auc), worst_auc = min(g$auc),
             auc_range_across_grid = max(g$auc) - min(g$auc))
}))
tuning_summary <- merge(tuning_summary, comparison[, .(model_id, hyperparameters)], by = "model_id")
knitr::kable(tuning_summary, digits = 5,
             caption = "AUC spread across each Stage 7 grid (small spread = flat response)")
```

## Comparative figures: dot plots

Dot plots are used for the metric comparisons because the AUC values differ in the third decimal; bars starting at zero would hide the differences. KNN is marked with an asterisk because it is scored on a subsample.

```{r figure-helpers}
plot_dt <- merge(tuned_metrics, models[, .(model_id, label)], by = "model_id")
plot_dt[, label_f := paste0(label, fifelse(evaluated_on != "full validation", "*", ""))]

metric_plot <- function(dt, metric, title, note) {
  d <- copy(dt)[, value := get(metric)]
  d[, label_f := factor(label_f, levels = d[order(value)]$label_f)]
  ggplot(d, aes(value, label_f, colour = evaluated_on)) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = min(value) - 0.5 * diff(range(value)), xend = value, yend = label_f), linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(size = 3.5) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.4f", value)), hjust = -0.35, size = 3.3, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.2))) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = note, x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL,
         caption = "* KNN scored on a 5,000-row validation subsample; others on full validation. Axis does not start at zero.") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```


## Comparative figures: ROC, Precision-Recall, confusion matrices, feature importance

These four are what Phase 2's own checklist asks for explicitly ("Comparative visualizations (ROC, Confusion Matrix, Feature Importance, Precision-Recall, etc.)") -- the dot plots above cover the same information numerically, these cover it the way the brief asks for.

```{r roc-pr-data}
curve_data <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(models)), function(i) {
  p <- preds[[models$tuned_col[i]]]
  keep <- which(!is.na(p))
  lbl <- plot_dt[model_id == models$model_id[i], label_f]
  roc_pts <- roc_curve_points(y[keep], p[keep])[, `:=`(curve = "roc", label = lbl)]
  pr_pts  <- pr_curve_points(y[keep], p[keep])[, `:=`(curve = "pr", label = lbl)]
  rbindlist(list(roc_pts, pr_pts), fill = TRUE)
}))
fwrite(curve_data, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "model_roc_pr_curve_points.csv"))
```

```{r fig-roc}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
p_roc <- ggplot(curve_data[curve == "roc"], aes(fpr, tpr, colour = label)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "ROC curves — tuned models (validation)",
       subtitle = "Dashed line = random-chance classifier",
       x = "False Positive Rate", y = "True Positive Rate", colour = NULL,
       caption = "KNN's curve uses its 5,000-row subsample; the others use full validation.") +
  coord_equal() + theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave(file.path(FIGURE_DIR, "model_roc_curves.png"), p_roc, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 200)
p_roc
```

```{r fig-pr}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
prevalence <- mean(y)
p_pr_curve <- ggplot(curve_data[curve == "pr"], aes(recall, precision, colour = label)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = prevalence, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Precision-Recall curves — tuned models (validation)",
       subtitle = paste0("Dashed line = no-skill baseline (prevalence = ", round(prevalence, 3), ")"),
       x = "Recall", y = "Precision", colour = NULL,
       caption = "KNN's curve uses its 5,000-row subsample; the others use full validation.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave(file.path(FIGURE_DIR, "model_pr_curves.png"), p_pr_curve, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 200)
p_pr_curve
```

```{r fig-confusion}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
confusion_data <- rbindlist(lapply(selection[selected == TRUE, model_id], function(id) {
  p <- preds[[models[model_id == id, tuned_col]]]
  keep <- which(!is.na(p))
  pred <- as.integer(p[keep] >= 0.5)
  tab <- as.data.table(table(Actual = y[keep], Predicted = pred))
  tab[, model_id := id]
  tab
}))
confusion_data <- merge(confusion_data, models[, .(model_id, label)], by = "model_id")
confusion_data[, Actual := factor(Actual, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Retained", "Returned"))]
confusion_data[, Predicted := factor(Predicted, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Retained", "Returned"))]
fwrite(confusion_data, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "model_confusion_matrix_counts.csv"))

p_confusion <- ggplot(confusion_data, aes(Predicted, Actual, fill = N)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = N), colour = "white", size = 4.2, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ label) +
  labs(title = "Confusion matrices at threshold 0.5 (selected models, full validation)",
       subtitle = "Threshold 0.5 is a reference point only -- Phase 3's CRC policy threshold is value-weighted and category-aware, not 0.5",
       x = "Predicted", y = "Actual") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
ggsave(file.path(FIGURE_DIR, "model_confusion_matrices.png"), p_confusion, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 200)
p_confusion
```

### Feature importance

**Limitation, stated plainly:** Random Forest has no extractable feature importance here. Stage 6's and Stage 7's `ranger()` calls never set `importance = "permutation"` (or `"impurity"`) at fit time, and `ranger` does not compute it retroactively from a fitted object -- recovering it would mean refitting the model, which needs the raw training pool this stage does not load. KNN fundamentally has no global feature-importance concept (it is a lazy, instance-based learner with no fitted weights). Both are therefore skipped below rather than faked.

```{r fig-xgboost-importance}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
xgb_importance <- tryCatch({
  xgb_fit <- readRDS(models[model_id == "xgboost", model_path])
  imp <- as.data.table(xgboost::xgb.importance(model = xgb_fit))
  imp[order(-Gain)][seq_len(min(15, .N))]
}, error = function(e) { cat("WARN: could not extract XGBoost importance:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })

if (!is.null(xgb_importance)) {
  fwrite(xgb_importance, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "model_xgboost_importance.csv"))
  p_xgb_imp <- ggplot(xgb_importance, aes(x = reorder(Feature, Gain), y = Gain)) +
    geom_col(fill = "#4C72B0") + coord_flip() +
    labs(title = "XGBoost feature importance (Gain)", x = NULL, y = "Gain") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
  ggsave(file.path(FIGURE_DIR, "model_xgboost_importance.png"), p_xgb_imp, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 200)
  p_xgb_imp
}
```

```{r fig-elasticnet-importance}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
elastic_importance <- tryCatch({
  en_fit <- readRDS(models[model_id == "elastic_net_logistic", model_path])
  coefs <- as.matrix(coef(en_fit$model, s = en_fit$lambda))
  dt <- data.table(feature = rownames(coefs), coefficient = coefs[, 1])[feature != "(Intercept)"]
  dt[order(-abs(coefficient))][seq_len(min(15, .N))]
}, error = function(e) { cat("WARN: could not extract Elastic-Net coefficients:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })

if (!is.null(elastic_importance)) {
  fwrite(elastic_importance, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "model_elastic_net_importance.csv"))
  p_en_imp <- ggplot(elastic_importance, aes(x = reorder(feature, coefficient), y = coefficient, fill = coefficient > 0)) +
    geom_col() + coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#C44E52", `FALSE` = "#4C72B0"), guide = "none") +
    labs(title = "Elastic-Net coefficient ranking (standardized predictors)",
         subtitle = "Red = pushes toward 'returned', blue = pushes toward 'retained'", x = NULL, y = "Coefficient") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
  ggsave(file.path(FIGURE_DIR, "model_elastic_net_importance.png"), p_en_imp, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 200)
  p_en_imp
}
```

## Model registry for Phase 3

```{r registry}
xgb_ubj <- file.path(MODEL_ZOO_TUNED_DIR, "xgboost_tuned.ubj")
tryCatch(xgboost::xgb.save(readRDS(models[model_id == "xgboost", model_path]), xgb_ubj),
         error = function(e) {
           xgb_ubj <<- NA_character_
           cat("WARN: could not write XGBoost .ubj copy:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
         })

registry <- list(
  created = Sys.time(),
  selection_basis = paste0("Validation split only; margin ", SELECTION_MARGIN, " AUC vs best"),
  validation_used_for_tuning = TRUE,
  note = paste("Tuned probabilities are NOT independent of the validation split.",
               "Calibrate / run CRC on crc_calibration, evaluate on iid_holdout, audit on future_test."),
  best_model = best_id,
  models = lapply(seq_len(nrow(selection)), function(i) {
    id <- selection$model_id[i]
    list(model_id = id, label = selection$label[i], selected = selection$selected[i],
         reason = selection$reason[i], validation_auc = selection$auc[i],
         validation_brier = selection$brier[i], evaluated_on = selection$evaluated_on[i],
         hyperparameters = comparison[model_id == id, hyperparameters],
         model_path = models[model_id == id, model_path],
         xgb_ubj_path = if (id == "xgboost") xgb_ubj else NA_character_,
         tuned_prob_column = models[model_id == id, tuned_col])
  })
)
saveRDS(registry, file.path(MODEL_DIR, "r_final_model_registry.rds"))
cat("Selected for Phase 3:", paste(selection[selected == TRUE, label], collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Stage 8 quality gate

```{r quality-gate}
cat("============================================================\nSTAGE 8 QUALITY GATE\n",
    "============================================================\n\n", sep = "")
GATE_PASS <- TRUE
fail_check <- function(msg) { cat("FAIL:", msg, "\n"); GATE_PASS <<- FALSE }
warn_check <- function(msg) cat("WARN:", msg, "\n")
pass_check <- function(msg) cat("PASS:", msg, "\n")

tables <- c("model_comparison_baseline_vs_tuned", "model_final_selection",
            "model_performance_comparison", "model_tuning_summary")
if (all(file.exists(file.path(TABLE_DIR, paste0(tables, ".csv"))))) pass_check("All 4 Stage 8 summary tables written.") else fail_check("A Stage 8 summary table is missing.")

required_figs <- c("model_auc_comparison", "model_brier_comparison", "model_pr_auc_comparison",
                    "model_tuning_gain", "model_roc_curves", "model_pr_curves", "model_confusion_matrices")
if (all(file.exists(file.path(FIGURE_DIR, paste0(required_figs, ".png"))))) pass_check("All 7 required figures written (dot plots + ROC/PR/confusion matrix).") else fail_check("A required figure is missing.")

optional_importance_figs <- c("model_xgboost_importance", "model_elastic_net_importance")
present_importance <- file.exists(file.path(FIGURE_DIR, paste0(optional_importance_figs, ".png")))
if (all(present_importance)) pass_check("Both feature-importance figures (XGBoost, Elastic-Net) written.") else warn_check("At least one feature-importance figure is missing -- check the WARN messages above for the extraction error.")

if (nrow(comparison) == 4) pass_check("Comparison has all 4 models.") else fail_check("Comparison does not have 4 models.")
chk <- merge(comparison[, .(model_id, tuned_auc)], stage7_comparison[, .(model_id, s7 = tuned_auc)], by = "model_id")
if (all(abs(chk$tuned_auc - chk$s7) < 1e-6)) pass_check("Recomputed tuned AUCs match Stage 7's table.") else fail_check("Recomputed tuned AUC differs from tune_05_baseline_vs_tuned.csv; prediction file or row order is off.")
if (abs(fast_auc(y, P[, 1]) - tuned_metrics[model_id == full_ids[1], auc]) < 1e-6) pass_check("Rank-based AUC agrees with auc_roc().") else warn_check("fast_auc() and auc_roc() disagree; bootstrap CIs may be slightly off.")

if (sum(selection$selected) >= 2) pass_check(paste(sum(selection$selected), "models selected for Phase 3.")) else warn_check("Fewer than 2 models selected.")
if (any(selection[selected == TRUE, evaluated_on] != "full validation")) fail_check("A subsample-evaluated model was selected.") else pass_check("Every selected model was scored on full validation.")
if (all(file.exists(models[model_id %in% selection[selected == TRUE, model_id], model_path]))) pass_check("Selected model files exist.") else fail_check("A selected model file is missing.")
if (file.exists(file.path(MODEL_DIR, "r_final_model_registry.rds"))) pass_check("Model registry saved.") else fail_check("Registry not saved.")

if (!is.null(knn_baseline_check) && !isTRUE(knn_baseline_check$same_rows)) warn_check("Baseline KNN was not scored on the same rows as tuned KNN; its auc_delta is not like-for-like.")
if (is.null(knn_baseline_check)) warn_check("KNN baseline rows unverified; do not quote the KNN tuning gain as exact.")
if (any(boot_tbl$gap_ci_low > 0)) warn_check("Some models have an AUC gap to the best whose 95% CI excludes 0: small but statistically detectable.")

if (!GATE_PASS) stop("Stage 8 quality gate failed -- see FAIL messages above.")
cat("\nAll required checks passed.\n")
```

## Handoff to Phase 3

The selected models and their tuned hyperparameters are recorded in `models/r_final_model_registry.rds`. Their tuned probabilities are not independent of `validation`, so Phase 3 calibrates on `crc_calibration`, evaluates on `iid_holdout`, and audits drift on `future_test`.

## Limitations

- All hyperparameters, including XGBoost's early-stopping round count, were chosen on `validation`, so tuned validation metrics are mildly optimistic.
- KNN was tuned and scored on a 5,000-row validation subsample with an 8,000-row training subsample, so its metrics are not directly comparable to the other models'.
- Several optima sat on grid boundaries (KNN k, XGBoost max_depth and eta, Random Forest mtry and min.node.size), so wider grids might give small further gains.
- The selection margin (`r SELECTION_MARGIN` AUC) is a judgment call; gaps inside it may still be statistically detectable (see the bootstrap table).
- Random Forest and KNN have no feature-importance figure (see the note above the importance plots) -- this is a genuine gap in what Stage 6/7 saved, not an oversight here.
- The confusion matrices use threshold 0.5 purely as a conventional reference point; it is not the project's actual decision rule (that is Phase 1's value-weighted, category-aware CRC threshold).
